opening: The road out was a thing you built, piece by piece, out of a city that was not going to offer you one.

clauses.text: You did not leave in one piece. You left carrying what the last week had put in you, and you left, which was the only part that was ever negotiable.
You went out whole — no fever, no wound worth naming, nothing owed to the road ahead. Almost nobody gets that.
Whatever is in your blood came with you past the last checkpoint, and it does not care that the city is behind you.
You left a house behind you with the door shut and the rooms still in it, and somebody will find it and think they were lucky.
The nights you spent holding those walls were what bought the time the work took.
You did not talk your way out of anything. Every hour of it was paid for the same way.
It took long enough that there were days you stopped believing in the road at all and kept working on it anyway.
You were gone before the city had finished deciding what to do about you.
Behind you the map went on emptying out. Not one of the people it emptied of had anywhere to go.
You are taking nothing out of there that you would have to explain, and that will matter later, on the nights it comes back.
You are taking some things out of there with you that are not in the pack, and those will keep.
You did not go alone. Whatever is out there, there is somebody to see it with.
You went alone. There was nobody left to ask, by then.
